Lenore — thanks for the clear ask. High level summary below, and Jordan/Kimberly are looped for the TIA/DTIA specifics and evidence pack.

1) Failover policy (short):
- Primary: EU West cluster (Frankfurt) handles production.
- Secondary (UK): we failover to our UK-only cluster (London) when region-level capacity or outage is detected AND the customer has "UK fallback" enabled in their routing policy. This preserves data locality in UK for customers who require it.
- Tertiary (US): only used for disaster recovery where both EU and UK are unavailable (extremely rare). In that case, data is encrypted in transit and at rest; we maintain an access log and limited retention on replication traffic.

2) Logs / telemetry:
- Application logs that contain PII are scrubbed before being sent to centralized analytics. Operational traces (non-PII) may flow through our aggregated monitoring pipeline; we can provide a filtered export showing no identifiable customer inputs.

3) Evidence for UK addendum signoff:
- We will produce: a) signed UK Addendum, b) dataflow map showing ingress/egress points, c) a short TIA statement that clarifies transient log flows and retention windows.

I've attached a 1-pager summary (redwood-failover-playbook-summary.pdf) and created HubSpot note RC-4598. Jordan — can you add the TIA language we propose and attach the redlined excerpt? Kimberly — can legal ops confirm the DocuSign sig block we should use.

Happy to jump on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Michael

Lenore / team — adding the TIA/DTIA technical clarifications below (draft language you can drop into the addendum):

Proposed TIA excerpt (draft):
"Redwood Inference confirms that for RetailCorp workloads with EU residency: 
(1) primary processing occurs in the designated EEA region; 
(2) automated failover to the United Kingdom region will only occur under the conditions described in the Routing Policy (capacity outage or regional unavailability) and will be limited to the subset of services explicitly enabled by the customer; 
(3) transient operational telemetry (traces/metrics) required for platform integrity may traverse Redwood-managed telemetry collectors located in EEA or UK and will be retained for no longer than 30 days unless otherwise agreed in writing; 
(4) persistent customer data will never be replicated outside the EEA/UK except as part of a documented DR event and only with provided contractual safeguards."

Notes: we have prepared a lightweight dataflow diagram attached (retailcorp-dataflow-map.pdf) that highlights egress nodes, ahead of signing. On logs: we can produce an extract showing sanitized trace headers and egress timestamps for your audit.

Question for RetailCorp: do you require the full UK IDTA or is the UK Addendum + above TIA language sufficient for your internal counsel?

Attached: retailcorp-dataflow-map.pdf (calls out the monitoring collectors and backup replication routes).
